newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-SENIOR STORMS AHEAD AFTER THIRD-ROUND 66.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SENIOR STORMS AHEAD AFTER THIRD-ROUND 66.

text.p: Australia's Peter Senior fired a third round of six-under-par 66 on Saturday to take the outright lead in the New South Wales Challenge and move into contention for a place in this year's British Open.
Senior's 66 saw him leapfrog a group of five overnight leaders and set up a two-stroke buffer, on 12-under 204, over compatriot David Ecob ahead of Sunday's final round at the Terrey Hills course.
Ecob birdied the final hole with a two-metre putt for a round of 69 to put himself two shots ahead of fellow Australian Robert Allenby.
Australians Peter Lonard, Chris Gray, Lucas Parsons and Stuart Bouvier, New Zealand's Steve Alker and Tsuyoshi Yoneyama of Japan were all another shot back on 209.
The top three players on this season's Australasian PGA Tour Order of Merit will qualify for exemptions into the British Open at Royal Troon in July.

A win on Sunday would see Senior bump world number one Greg Norman out of third place on the Order of Merit. Senior's previous best result at the British Open was fourth behind Norman at Royal St George's in 1993.
Senior, a regular on the European and Japanese tours, had seven birdies with putts of between three and six metres.
"I played better than I have for a long, long time," Senior said.
Senior's only blemish came with a bogey five on the final hole after his tee shot found thick rough on the side of the fairway.
Ecob, who does not have a tour card outside Australia, stayed in contention with steady iron play after sharing the overnight lead.
Allenby picked up three birdies on his final six holes while Australian Masters champion Lonard, who had also shared the overnight lead, dropped down the leaderboard after a round of 72.
